disclaimer: All organisations, grants, events, species and relationships are wholly fictional. Real city coordinates are used only as a backdrop. All counts describe intended source interpretations; final visual support is tested separately.

examples.title: The Neighbourhood Web
examples.description: Seven fictional towns, hundreds of community organisations, shared projects and explicit partnerships.
examples.whatToTry: Find organisations that bridge otherwise separate areas. Then look at the same recorded links geographically.
examples.caveat: Closeness on the diagram isn't proof of collaboration; the source only records the links in the table.
observations: A few bridges between distant areas

examples.title: After Hours: Culture Across Places
examples.description: Venues, promoters and recorded touring or collaboration links across seven real UK cities; every organisation and relationship is fictional.
examples.whatToTry: Switch between points and connected arcs; trace who bridges different towns.
examples.caveat: The venues and promoters are inventions, even though the geographic backdrop uses real city locations.

examples.title: Six Years of Community Funding
examples.description: An invented grants portfolio with repeat awards, unequal funder reach, programme shifts and distinct funding sizes.
examples.whatToTry: Compare funders, award amounts, recipients and how the priorities move between years.
examples.caveat: Shared recipients or a common funder do not demonstrate organisations working together.
observations: Small awards sit alongside major investments

examples.title: How Food Moves
examples.description: Fictional farms, community kitchens and food hubs with hundreds of explicit supply and distribution routes.
examples.whatToTry: Find fragile hubs, trace recorded routes and compare local clusters to cross-area deliveries.
examples.caveat: A source-recorded supply relationship isn't evidence of a quantity, value or successful delivery without those fields.

examples.title: A Year of Community Activity
examples.description: Repeated sessions across four years, with organising bodies, places, topics and participant numbers.
examples.whatToTry: Explore which organisations appear most often, then compare seasons, topics and attendance once event charting lands.
examples.caveat: Appearing in a row with an event does not, alone, prove collaboration or wider impact.

examples.title: Living Places: Field Observations
examples.description: Hundreds of invented species observations at real geographic coordinates, with strong local and seasonal variation.
examples.whatToTry: Explore observation clusters, species concentrations and where the records are sparse.
examples.caveat: Observations are not proof of species absence elsewhere and don't create relationships between observations.
observations: Source dates available for further charting

examples.title: Common Ground: A Project Portfolio
examples.description: A portfolio of projects across places with overlapping source-given themes and year fields, but no asserted partnerships.
examples.whatToTry: See themes that recur, try different groupings and inspect projects within each group.
examples.caveat: Sharing a tag is not evidence of partnership. No links have been fabricated in this dataset.

examples.title: A Patchwork of Projects
examples.description: Different file types forming one picture: a CSV organisation register, nested JSON initiatives and a separate connection list.
examples.whatToTry: Compare sources, follow who works across initiatives and inspect the original rows behind the links.
examples.caveat: Cross-file records must not merge merely because they share a similar name or location.
observations: Repeated themes and distinct source receipts
